local_facts.claim: Louisiana Civil Code article 3493.1 now gives delictual actions a two-year liberative prescription beginning the day injury or damage is sustained. Acts 2024, No. 423 made the current rule effective July 1, 2024; the former one-year rule is not the current period for a new ordinary injury claim.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Louisiana uses the civil-law term prescription rather than statute of limitations. A rider who acts on an old one-year warning may make rushed decisions, while a rider who merely assumes a carrier will keep the file open can still lose a two-year claim. The crash date and any special notice rules need to be identified early.
local_facts.title: Louisiana's current ordinary injury period is two years

local_facts.claim: Under the current version of Civil Code article 2323, effective January 1, 2026, a claimant assigned less than 51% fault has damages reduced proportionally; a claimant assigned 51% or more cannot recover damages. Orleans Parish Civil District Court is located at 421 Loyola Avenue in New Orleans.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The old description of Louisiana as a pure comparative-fault state is outdated. In a motorcycle claim, evidence about each person's movement and the rider's available path can directly affect recovery. A qualifying Orleans Parish civil case is handled in Civil District Court, though venue depends on the specific facts and parties.
local_facts.title: Current fault rule and Orleans Parish civil venue

local_facts.claim: The City says subsidence occurs throughout the New Orleans planning area and has caused extensive road and drainage-system damage. Its citywide pavement assessment reported roughly 65% of streets in poor-or-worse condition; New Orleans also operates streetcar tracks that require particular attention around crossings.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A motorcycle claim may turn on the rider's escape path as well as the other driver's movement. Broken pavement, drainage features, and streetcar rails should be photographed in context before weather, traffic, or repairs change the scene. A bad street alone does not decide liability, but it can be important evidence.
local_facts.title: Subsidence, pavement failure, and tracks are real scene evidence

anchors.label: Percentage ceiling on a crash claim fee
anchors.detail: Rule 1.5 tests a fee for reasonableness against eight factors and permits a contingent fee in a civil matter. It publishes no percentage.

anchors.label: Prescriptive period for a delictual action
anchors.detail: Running from the day the injury or damage is sustained, under the period enacted by Acts 2024, No. 423, effective July 1, 2024.

anchors.label: Claimant fault that bars recovery outright
anchors.detail: Recovery is barred where the injured person's share of fault is equal to or greater than fifty-one percent, under the amendment effective January 1, 2026.

anchors.label: Plaintiff's filing fee on an original petition
anchors.detail: Orleans Parish Civil District Court, effective July 1, 2026: a $489.50 filing fee plus a $25 building fee. A request for trial by jury is $780 more.
anchors.source_name: Orleans Parish Clerk of Civil District Court fee schedule

fee_rows.stage: The fee on a motorcycle claim
fee_rows.share: Set by agreement, tested for reasonableness
fee_rows.note: Rule 1.5(a) forbids an unreasonable fee and lists the factors used to measure one. Nothing in the rule states a percentage a Louisiana lawyer must charge.

Paragraph (c) requires a writing signed by the client with a copy handed over at signing, the percentages for settlement, trial and appeal, the expenses deducted, whether they come off before or after the fee, and a closing written statement.

fee_rows.stage: The lawyer's claim on the recovery
fee_rows.note: By written contract signed by the client, an attorney may acquire an interest in the subject matter that ranks as a first privilege superior to other privileges and security interests.
A provider privilege attaches to the net amount payable to the injured person out of any recovery, and the statute states that an attorney's privilege takes precedence over it.

fee_rows.stage: Opening the suit in Orleans Parish
fee_rows.note: Original petition, an amending or supplemental petition, and a request for trial by jury. Naming more than five defendants adds $132 and a petition of intervention is $234.50.
fee_rows.source_name: Orleans Parish Clerk of Civil District Court fee schedule

fee_rows.stage: Cash deposit to hold a jury
fee_rows.note: In a damages suit where an individual petitioner admits the cause of action exceeds $10,000 and is less than $50,000, the deposit is due within sixty days of the jury request or the jury is waived.
